notes: Suit on a multi-year agricultural plantation lease and suretyship for rent notes; concerns overflow abatement, surety discharge by prolongation, and administratrix authority. No occupancy-of-dwelling/lodging issue.

Plaintiff leased the Orleans Hotel building itself (as hotel-keeper/lessee) from the owners; dispute is over landlord's duty to repair the leased premises and lessee's damages claim, not over the character of guest lodging arrangements or room-letting by a householder.

cite: Bienvenu v. Factors' & Traders' Insurance, 33 La. Ann. 209
notes: Appellate procedure (motion to dismiss appeal) and a mortgage/partition dispute over undivided lot interests; terminology dispute is over 'curator ad hoc' vs 'attorney ad hoc', unrelated to lodging or letting.

cite: Crescent City Live Stock Landing & Slaughter-House Co. v. City of New Orleans, 33 La. Ann. 934
notes: Police-power case on the state's authority to revoke a slaughterhouse monopoly charter under the 1879 Constitution. Discusses police power generally but has no bearing on lodging/boarding-house regulation or residential letting.

cite: Todd v. Richmond, 1 Mann. Unrep. Cas. 268
notes: Venue/jurisdiction and third-opposition procedure dispute over a purchased judgment/mortgage interest, and whether the claim purchased was a prohibited litigious right. No letting or lodging issue.

cite: Randolph v. Wood, 1 Mann. Unrep. Cas. 324
notes: Riparian-rights dispute over mooring piles and coal-barge landing on a riverbank; no rent recoverable for such temporary bank use. Unrelated to dwelling/room letting.

cite: Heirs of Prudhomme v. Walmsley, 1 Mann. Unrep. Cas. 374
notes: Ejectment of a lessee from the Panola plantation (agricultural lease, tacit reconduction) and procedure on jury trial/damages claims. Not a dwelling/lodging letting case.

cite: New Orleans v. Campbell, 1 Mann. Unrep. Cas. 47
notes: Long-term (50-year) ground lease of vacant lots to a lessee who built improvements, and tax-exemption/mortgageability of the lessee's rights vis-a-vis a charitable lessor (orphan asylum). Not about residential lodging or room-letting.

cite: Joseph Landis & Co. v. Walker, 15 La. Ann. 213
notes: Domicile/venue dispute plus a commission-agent/factor's suit over molasses consignments. No letting of dwellings or rooms.

Wife held a ground lease on which she built wooden structures and sub-leased them at a profit; dispute is whether the lease/buildings were her paraphernal property or community-debt-liable. The sub-lease appears to be of whole buildings for profit as an investment, not room/lodging letting in a dwelling, and the court does not characterize the arrangement doctrinally as lease/license/lodging.

cite: State ex rel. Rutherford v. Third Justice of the Peace, 15 La. Ann. 660
notes: Jurisdictional dispute over Justice of the Peace authority to hear a landlord-tenant ejectment where two whole houses on one lot, jointly leased at $125/month, passed to separate owners on partition. Ordinary whole-building lease/ejectment jurisdiction question, not a lodger/boarder or short-term room-letting case; no characterization quote of the kind required is present.
Petitory (title) action against a lessee/agent in possession of a tract of land; holds lessee lacks capacity to litigate title. Rural land title dispute, not dwelling/room letting.

cite: State v. City of New Orleans, 15 La. Ann. 354
notes: Constitutional dispute over legislative control of city election administration and definition of 'police' power/taxation; extensive general discussion of the meaning of 'police' but nothing about lodging houses, boarders, or dwelling letting.

cite: Jenkins v. New Orleans, Opelousas & Great Western Railroad, 15 La. Ann. 118
notes: Cattle-trespass/railroad-collision liability dispute; wholly unrelated to letting or lodging.
Partition action over slaves inherited from a community estate; succession/family-meeting adjudication procedure. No letting or lodging issue.

General lease-formation doctrine case (thing, price, consent required; mere occupancy doesn't prove lessor/lessee relation) arising from a lessor's-privilege claim over farm/plantation land and movables. States a generic lease doctrine but the underlying facts involve land/movables, not dwelling rooms or lodgers; not on point for the householder/boarding-house question.

Dispute over a parish police jury's power to levy taxes within an incorporated town under its charter. Uses 'police' in the sense of local governmental power, unrelated to lodging-house regulation or letting.

Commercial store lease/sublease dispute over the lessor's privilege on a judgment debtor's merchandise seized on the leased premises; concerns priority of creditors' claims to sale proceeds, not dwelling occupancy or lodging.
